title: What von der Leyen’s SOTU speech got right about energy—and where the EU still needs to pivot
gist: Two Atlantic Council experts assess von der Leyen's September 16 SOTU: correct diagnosis that structurally high energy prices threaten EU industry, but delivery lags targets; the heatwave plan, a Canada 'associate member' energy/minerals alliance and a European Corporation on Critical Raw Materials are the key new moves, while Hormuz has cost Europe an extra EUR 90 billion in fuel imports.

insights.claim: Structurally high energy prices mean Europe cannot sustain either a strong industrial base or public support for the energy transition.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Energy costs remain the binding constraint for European industrials — a persistent headwind for energy-intensive sectors.
insights.locator: Ursula von der Leyen’s speech accurately identifies

insights.claim: After Russian gas dependence and the Strait of Hormuz disruption, a gallon of diesel in Germany now costs more than $10.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Extreme diesel prices signal refining/middle-distillate tightness in Europe — watch margins and demand destruction.

insights.claim: Von der Leyen said this year's Hormuz closure has cost Europe an additional EUR 90 billion in imported fossil fuels without adding any energy.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Quantifies the terms-of-trade hit to Europe — negative for EU current account and euro-area growth.
insights.quote: without a single molecule of energy added
insights.locator: In her EU State of the Union address

insights.claim: Europe is addicted to setting ambitious climate targets rather than delivering them; the technology-neutral approach von der Leyen advocates is still not implemented across EU institutions.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Policy-execution risk: don't bank on announced EU targets translating into capacity on schedule.
insights.quote: Europe is addicted to setting ambitious targets rather than delivering them.

insights.claim: Lowering European energy prices requires a policy shift followed by investment, cross-border interconnections, faster decisions and fair distribution of transition costs, not declarations.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Grid interconnection and permitting reform are the investable levers if the EU follows through.
insights.locator: Europe will not bring down energy prices

insights.claim: Grids, terminals, storage facilities and digital control systems are strategic infrastructure whose protection against sabotage and cyberattacks must become part of European security planning.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Tailwind for infrastructure security and OT cybersecurity spending in Europe.
insights.locator: This challenge must also be viewed

insights.claim: Europe's summer heat forced nuclear units in Hungary and Romania offline as the Danube ran low, and pushed cooling demand through buildings designed to retain heat.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Water-constrained thermal/nuclear generation is a growing summer supply risk — supports summer power price spikes.

insights.claim: A heatwave is a compound stress event hitting generation, networks and consumption simultaneously, not merely a demand event; Europe has a heating strategy but no cooling plan.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Model summer power risk as correlated supply-and-demand shocks, not just demand peaks.
insights.quote: A heatwave is not a demand event; it is a compound stress event that hits energy generation, networks, and consumption at once.

insights.claim: The SOTU announced a European Heatwave Plan and a climate resilience framework due next month; only a quarter of Europe's catastrophe losses are insured, linking the plan to the Climate Insurance Alliance.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Large protection gap is an opportunity/risk for insurers and reinsurers in Europe.

insights.claim: Cooling, water and energy costs are aimed at voters ahead of 2027 elections in France, Spain and Italy, where challengers target energy costs and Brussels.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Energy affordability is a political risk factor for 2027 European elections — watch populist gains and fiscal energy subsidies.
insights.locator: Finally, no policy speech would be complete

insights.claim: The EU opened the door for Canada to become its first 'associate member', with a proposed Alliance for the Future prioritising energy, critical minerals and batteries; next month's EU-Canada summit in Montreal is the test.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Canadian uranium, LNG and critical-minerals producers could gain EU offtake and joint procurement.

insights.claim: Canada is one of the world's largest uranium producers and a potential LNG supplier to the EU.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Supports the investment case for Canadian uranium and LNG export projects tied to European demand.

insights.claim: Washington is reportedly weighing restrictions on exports of refined products, above all diesel, to ease domestic prices before the midterms, which would hit European buyers who turned to US barrels after the Russian ban.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: A US product-export curb would widen transatlantic diesel spreads and squeeze European supply — key risk for refiners and distillate cracks.

insights.claim: European energy sovereignty should mean building stable partnerships with the US, Canada, Norway, the UK and Australia while pairing protective instruments with dialogue toward China.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Suggests supplier diversification toward allied producers rather than autarky.

themes.theme: Critical raw materials dependence on China

insights.claim: Europe is more than 80% dependent on China for many critical raw materials and 90% for some rare earths; von der Leyen announced a European Corporation on Critical Raw Materials to secure and stockpile them.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
entities: European Corporation on Critical Raw Materials
insights.so_what: New EU buyer/stockpiler for critical minerals — supportive demand for non-Chinese supply.
insights.locator: Partners matter as much for minerals

insights.claim: Stockpiles buy time but not independence, because Europe's exposure is in processing and refining where China holds leverage ahead of the October deadline in EU-China trade talks.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Invest in non-Chinese midstream processing; offtake guarantees matter more than stockpiles.
insights.quote: But stockpiles buy time, not independence.
insights.locator: Partners matter as much for minerals
